Just 10 stocks have driven 70% of the S&P 500’s gain since March 30th.

Diversification is dead.

The global debt crisis is set to get even worse:

The US fiscal deficit is projected to widen to -6.1% of GDP in 2027, its largest since 2012, excluding the pandemic years of 2020 and 2021.

This will be the biggest deficit as a % of GDP among the 5 major developed economies, including the UK, Germany, France, and Japan.

Furthermore, Germany's deficit is expected to widen from -2.7% of GDP in 2025 to -4.1% in 2027, its largest since 2010, excluding the 2020 pandemic.

Japan's fiscal deficit is estimated to more than triple, from -0.7% to -2.5% of GDP, its largest since 2022.

The UK is the only economy expected to improve its fiscal position, with its deficit narrowing from -4.3% in 2025, to -3.1% of GDP next year, while France's budget gap is projected to widen to -5.2%.

Deficit spending is only accelerating.

a16z crypto's Eddy Lazzarin on why AI makes the world more secure: bugs are finite, and the cost of finding them keeps collapsing.

"Making comparisons between models from a year ago versus today... Some people were coming up with estimates like it's... 99% cheaper for intellectual capability per dollar."

"Pair that with a frame we've talked about before, which is that the number of bugs in software is finite. Then we're asymptotically approaching zero bugs. Maybe we actually just hit zero at some point."

"If that's the case, we are net improving the security status of the world instead of eroding it."

"This is not a battle of wits where you have a system, I have a system, your system is smarter than mine, therefore I am vulnerable to you... That relies on there being vulnerabilities, and vulnerabilities can be removed."

"The primary resource we dedicate to mitigating it is a thing that's getting radically cheaper every couple months. That's AI."

Dan Boneh: "Companies actually are already doing this. They're spending a lot of money on scanning their code base with the latest models... Every time there's a software update... Every time a new model comes out, they scan the software again."

@eddylazzarin @danboneh

A story can take a company public, and even take it a little bit farther than that for a while but eventually cash flow and actual growth is what keeps it there, and Beyond has never had it. $BYND

⚠️ 🇺🇲 House Democrats plan a first 100-days agenda if they sweep to power in midterm elections - AP

➡️ Democrats are preparing an aggressive post-midterm agenda: If they regain control of the House, they plan to challenge Trump's tariffs, reverse healthcare cuts, push to end the Iran war, and launch extensive investigations into his administration.

➡️ Political gridlock is the most likely outcome: Even with a Democratic House majority, Trump's veto power and potential Republican control of the Senate would severely limit Democrats' ability to reverse his policies. Expect more confrontation than actual legislative change.

➡️ AI infrastructure could become a major political target: Democrats' focus on affordability increasingly conflicts with the massive electricity demand and infrastructure costs associated with data centers. Hyperscalers could face greater scrutiny over energy pricing, financing structures, and infrastructure development.

➡️ The AI capex cycle is unlikely to collapse, but risks are rising: Additional regulatory pressure, higher energy costs, and permitting constraints could weaken project economics and make hyperscalers more selective with their investments, potentially affecting the broader AI supply chain.

➡️ Market implications are mixed: Lower tariffs and a potential de-escalation in Iran could ease inflationary pressures, while increased regulatory scrutiny and budgetary uncertainty could weigh on corporate earnings expectations.

➡️ Democrats' economic agenda remains relatively weak: Their proposals largely focus on reversing Trump's policies rather than addressing structural challenges such as housing affordability, elevated long-term interest rates, and persistent fiscal deficits.

➡️ Much of a Democratic House victory may already be priced in: The real market-moving developments will likely come after the election, particularly through congressional committee leadership, regulatory initiatives, and potential changes to corporate capex guidance.

⚠️ Bottom line: A Democratic victory would not necessarily derail Trump's economic agenda, but it could significantly increase political uncertainty around the AI investment boom. The biggest risk is not an immediate collapse in capex, but a gradual deterioration in the economics supporting today's aggressive AI growth expectations.

⚠️ 🇺🇲 House Democrats plan a first 100-days agenda if they sweep to power in midterm elections - AP

➡️ Democrats are preparing an aggressive post-midterm agenda: If they regain control of the House, they plan to challenge Trump's tariffs, reverse healthcare cuts, push to end the Iran war, and launch extensive investigations into his administration.

➡️ Political gridlock is the most likely outcome: Even with a Democratic House majority, Trump's veto power and potential Republican control of the Senate would severely limit Democrats' ability to reverse his policies. Expect more confrontation than actual legislative change.

➡️ AI infrastructure could become a major political target: Democrats' focus on affordability increasingly conflicts with the massive electricity demand and infrastructure costs associated with data centers. Hyperscalers could face greater scrutiny over energy pricing, financing structures, and infrastructure development.

➡️ The AI capex cycle is unlikely to collapse, but risks are rising: Additional regulatory pressure, higher energy costs, and permitting constraints could weaken project economics and make hyperscalers more selective with their investments, potentially affecting the broader AI supply chain.

➡️ Market implications are mixed: Lower tariffs and a potential de-escalation in Iran could ease inflationary pressures, while increased regulatory scrutiny and budgetary uncertainty could weigh on corporate earnings expectations.

➡️ Democrats' economic agenda remains relatively weak: Their proposals largely focus on reversing Trump's policies rather than addressing structural challenges such as housing affordability, elevated long-term interest rates, and persistent fiscal deficits.

➡️ Much of a Democratic House victory may already be priced in: The real market-moving developments will likely come after the election, particularly through congressional committee leadership, regulatory initiatives, and potential changes to corporate capex guidance.

⚠️ Bottom line: A Democratic victory would not necessarily derail Trump's economic agenda, but it could significantly increase political uncertainty around the AI investment boom. The biggest risk is not an immediate collapse in capex, but a gradual deterioration in the economics supporting today's aggressive AI growth expectations.
